verdict.rationale: Statsig documents programmatic flag management that an agent could drive: the Console API is a CRUD API for console actions, the CLI manages Feature Gates and plugs into CI/CD, and an official MCP server connects Statsig to Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. However, nothing in the evidence shows the governance half of the story, where agent-originated changes are forced through review or approval before reaching production. The MCP server is also described mainly in terms of asking questions and exploring data rather than writing flags. missing for 10: documented approval/review workflows that gate API/CLI/MCP flag changes, evidence the MCP server can create or toggle flags, policy controls preventing unreviewed production writes, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: The Console API is the CRUD API for performing the actions available on console.statsig.com without using the web UI.
The Statsig CLI is a command-line interface that helps manage Feature Gates, Experiments, and Dynamic Configs within the Statsig platform.
The Statsig MCP (Model Context Protocol) server brings the power of Statsig into tools like Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code.
